title: Nourishing Charred Uruguayan Flax Skillet
description: A kosher-friendly, indulgent Uruguayan dish featuring flax eggs, en-croute, and a glassy-jelly texture, all charred to perfection in an iron-teppan skillet.
instructions: Preheat the iron-teppan skillet over medium heat.
In a small bowl, mix together the ground flaxseed and water to create a flax egg, and let it sit for 5 minutes.
Add the olive oil to the preheated skillet and swirl it around to coat the bottom.
Add the chopped onion to the skillet and cook until it is translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic to the skillet and cook for an additional minute.
Add the chopped red bell pepper to the skillet and cook until it is tender, about 5 minutes.
Add the flax egg to the skillet and stir to combine with the vegetables.
Season the mixture with salt, black pepper, and paprika, and stir to combine.
Use a spatula to shape the mixture into a round, flat shape, and cook for an additional 5 minutes, until the bottom is charred and the top is set.
Use the spatula to carefully flip the skillet contents over and cook for an additional 2 minutes, until the other side is also charred.
Remove the skillet from the heat and let it cool for a few minutes before serving.
